history.origins: Trains is a modern American folk card game of the 20th century, played with a standard 52-card deck. It emerged as a casual, simultaneous-play climbing game in which players race to complete an ascending sequence (the Train) starting from a 2. No single published origin or inventor is documented; it is transmitted as a traditional family or social game.
timeline: 20th century: Modern folk card game in the USA; played with standard deck, simultaneous play to complete ascending Train from 2.

setup.dealing: Deal 7 cards. Remaining split into piles (4 in round 1, 3 in round 2, etc.).

rules.objective: Be first to complete a Train (ascending sequence from 2 using all cards).
rules.gameplay: Simultaneous play. Central area for played cards. Pile Play for building Train. Sandwiches (matching cards with filler) and Doubles are special plays.
keyRules: All cards in hand must be used

scoring.description: 1 point per round won. 4 rounds total.
scoring.winCondition: Be first to complete a Train (ascending sequence from 2 using all cards).
